clauses.text: Opinions for writing xUnit tests against an Entity Framework Core DbContext backed by SQLite.
Not for production code, migrations, or tests that do not touch a DbContext.

baseline: Write xUnit tests for Entity Framework Core code.

cases.prompt: Write xUnit tests for our OrderRepository. It uses AppDbContext and we run tests against in-memory SQLite.
Add a test that GetTopPosts returns posts in descending order of views. The method queries db.Posts.
These three tests each build their own BlogContext and SQLite connection. Clean up the duplication.
I need coverage for the cancel-order flow. It writes through AppDbContext and flips Order.Status.
Write a theory test for the paging logic of our post queries against the blogging DbContext.

Rename these xUnit tests so they read better. They seed and query a CustomerContext:
```csharp
[Fact] public async Task Test1() { /* seeds customers, queries by city */ }
```
Add tests for the new CustomerService. It takes our DbContext and saves orders.
Our integration tests for the Orders table are flaky because they share one database. Fix the fixture.
Test that deleting a Blog also deletes its Posts, using xUnit and EF Core.
Write tests for the method that totals Views per Blog. It reads from BlogContext.
Write xUnit tests for this pure function: static string Slugify(string title).
Write Jest tests for this React hook that debounces a value.
Write the repository method that returns posts with more than 100 views from our EF Core context.
Create an EF Core migration for the new Order.Status column.
Configure the Post to Blog relationship with the Fluent API and a cascade delete.
Write xUnit tests for PriceCalculator. It takes an IDiscountService that I want to mock with Moq.

Review this for problems:
```csharp
var posts = db.Posts.ToList().Where(p => p.Views > 100);
```
Explain what xUnit's [Theory] and [InlineData] attributes do.
Write a commit message for the test changes I have staged.
Write xUnit tests for a CSV line splitter that handles quoted commas.
This SQL query is slow. Which index should I add?
Write a Playwright end-to-end test for the login page.
